name: Edging — Approaching and Easing Away
summary: Edging means approaching orgasm and then easing away repeatedly, which builds longer, more intense orgasms for 65.5% of women by holding off climax before it happens. Three variations—pause, distraction, and continuous—suit different bodies and minds.
detailed_description: By walking up to the edge of orgasm and backing off, edging accumulates tension for a bigger eventual release. OMGYES describes three methods: pause edging (stop all touch), distraction edging (shift focus with sensation away from the clit), and continuous edging (move to non-clitoral touch without fully stopping). Lighter pressure near climax helps most people. It isn't for everyone—some can't rebuild after pausing and do better with the continuous variation, and a few find rebuilding to orgasm too hard to enjoy edging at all.
stepwise_structure: 1. Build arousal until orgasm feels close.
2. Just before climax, ease away using one of the three methods (pause, distraction, or continuous).
4. Return to stimulation and rebuild toward the edge again.
5. Repeat several times; reduce pressure near climax to make easing off easier.
6. Edge earlier in the session to avoid hitting an unstoppable point of no return.
safety_notes: Backing off when close is frustrating but normal—it's part of the technique.
If rebuilding after a pause fails, switch to continuous edging.
Edging isn't for everyone; stop if rebuilding to orgasm feels impossible or unpleasant.
Adults in consensual contexts only; not a substitute for professional care.
